precepts.text: Thou shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee, and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not. That is the lawsuit the Lord took out against the nation: you serve your enemies, you forget who you are, and you walk around blind.
precepts.point: The beasts of the field, the fowls of heaven and the fishes of the sea are taken away with us. The repercussions run past the people and into the land itself.

note.label: Blood Toucheth Blood

precepts.text: Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone. Ephraim is joined to idols. Let him alone. You get that in Santería, brujería, Catholicism. This is what our people are into.
precepts.point: Therefore the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only. So our people were always into idolatry.

note.label: Abya Yala Under Fire

precepts.why:
Kings tells what the northern kingdom did: “they left all the commandments of the Lord their God, and made them molten images, even two calves, and made a grove, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served Baal.” They made false gods; they served Satan, the devil. They caused their sons and daughters to pass through the fire: today we call it abortion, which is murder. They used divination and enchantments, witchcraft, and “sold themselves to do evil in the sight of the Lord”. So the Lord removed them out of his sight.

Our people were always into idolatry, and Hosea says it in one line: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” Joined to idols. Idols, idols, idols. Leave him alone.

And it is still so today. You get it in Santería, brujería, Catholicism; this is what our people, the northern kingdom, the so-called Latinos, are into. That is why the curses keep following us: we want to celebrate witchcraft and idolatry, and the Most High is jacking us up, with earthquakes, puppet presidents and our lands being taken. Why? Because we don't learn. It is all to bring us back to repentance and to the remembrance of who we are.

precepts.text: This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die. Such as leave it, or break away from it, shall die. That is what they break out means.
precepts.point: The truth for us is the only thing we have to get up out of here. This is all we have. There is no plan B. Outside of this is death. And what God is really asking of us is a small thing in comparison to the sins that we have committed. So what is hard about not stealing, not swearing, not lying, not committing adultery, keeping the Sabbath day holy? Those are minor things. Minor, in the scope of eternal life.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

precepts.why:
Hosea says of Israel that “they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” Baruch shows what breaking out is: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Such as leave the law, or break away from it, shall die. That is what they break out means.

So the sins Hosea lists, swearing, lying, killing, stealing and committing adultery, are a breaking away from the book of the commandments. Where the law is left, there is no truth, no mercy and no knowledge of God in the land, because truth is the application of God's laws, and the laws of God are not being taught or enforced.

And once they break out, blood toucheth blood: violence, hatred, killing against each other. The law endures for ever and keeping it is life; leaving it is death. The truth is the only thing we have to get up out of here. There is no plan B. Outside of this is death.

That is why the land mourns. If those same sins abide in the body, adultery, stealing, lying, swearing, not applying God's laws, hatred, violence, the congregation will not grow and will not flourish. As leaders we must teach the laws, hold people accountable to them, and be the example ourselves, so people can see there has to be a change in the way we move and how we think.

precepts.text: Can two walk together, except they be agreed? That is the answer to congregating with somebody who has been put out of the body.

And what God is really asking of us is a small thing in comparison to the sins that we have committed. note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

precepts.why:
“Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” That is the answer to the one who decides not to congregate with the body on the Sabbath, or to congregate partially, and then congregates with somebody that has been put out of the body. That is out of order, and it is sin.

The Sabbath is not negotiable: remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. We cannot cook, we cannot buy, we cannot sell on the Lord's Sabbath day, and we must congregate, because it is a holy convocation. There is no way around that; you cannot decide not to do it. It is those small things, the application of God's laws, that separate us.

People do otherwise because we rationalise in our minds what we think is acceptable and what God will be all right with. God said, No, my commandments are straight; this is what I told you to do. Our biggest problem is trying to put our own thoughts in on how it should be done, but the Lord said, Your thoughts are not my thoughts. It is not hard. It only gets hard when we start to rationalise.

Imagine if that is how we started, people coming and going, this one wearing a yarmulke, this one wearing that. That is not how you build God's army. There must be structure, and the leaders are the example, the representative of what a godly Israelite looks like. When there is no agreement in the body, there is no truth in the land, and the land mourns.

precepts.text: Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone. Cuz remember, Jeroboam set up priests in the land. So we did not deal with them.
precepts.point: And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him, and he abode there two days. If they weren't Israelites, why would he stay there and teach them for two days? It makes no sense. Now we believe, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world: of the world of Israel.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
After Christ dealt with Judah, “he must needs go through Samaria.” There the woman said, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” The southern kingdom did not deal with the northern kingdom. Remember the rift from Rehoboam; that was always the problem.

Hosea gives the reason: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” Remember, Jeroboam set up priests in the land, and Ephraim went into idolatry. So we did not deal with them.

But she was still an Israelite: “Art thou greater than our father Jacob”? Right there she's telling you she's an Israelite. People on YouTube say she wasn't, because Shalmaneser put men of Babylon and the Chaldees in the land, but there is more history: Ezra shows Israelites coming back to the land. And if she was lying about her identity, why didn't Christ correct her? He did correct her about something, her five husbands, letting her know she was living a whorish lifestyle, because sex does not constitute marriage. But he never corrected her nationality.

He revealed himself to her, “I that speak unto thee am he”, which he would not do if she were not an Israelite, and his disciples marvelled that he talked with her, because the Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans. Then he abode there two days teaching them, and they knew he was “the Saviour of the world”, the world of Israel. The one Hosea said to let alone, Christ went to gather.

precepts.text: And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. That was the promise made to us and our ancestors; that is the priesthood we were rejected from for forgetting the law.
precepts.point: Because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me. This is why other races come into our communities and run the hospitals, the stores, the clinics. Many of us do have the knowledge and ability, but they do not want us to have the capability.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me”. What does that part mean, that thou shalt be no priest to me?

There was a promise made to us and our ancestors: “And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.” A kingdom of priests. That is what Israel was called to be.

Go back to Hosea and it tells you why we lost it: “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God”. That is the knowledge. Usually we jump over to Malachi 2:7, but the verse tells you right there: the knowledge is the law of God, his laws, his commandments, his statutes. Because we forgot it, he rejected us from that priesthood.

That is why we are destroyed as a race, as a people, mentally and spiritually. The twelve tribes of Israel are a destroyed race. This is why other races come into our communities and run the hospitals, the stores, the clinics. The black man and the brown man do have the ability, and many of us have the knowledge to do it, but they do not want us to have the capabilities.

precepts.text: A brother answered why the Jews stopped dealing with them: Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.
precepts.point: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst, but it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they were disconnected from it for so long.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The woman of Samaria said, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” These Samaritans were Israelites who still lived there. Samaria is north of Jerusalem, as the map shows, and the Jews of Jerusalem stopped dealing with our people located in Samaria.

Why did that happen? A brother answered from Hosea: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” That is why she said it. The scripture said Ephraim was joined to idols, and the word was to let him alone.

So the separation between the Jews and the Samaritans was not just a grudge; it grew out of the judgment on the northern kingdom for its idolatry. Judah took that word and left Ephraim alone. Yet here Christ, of Judah, sits at Jacob's well and asks a woman of Samaria to give him drink.

Truth is the law, Psalms 119:142, and nobody in the land adheres to do not prostitute thy daughter; no mercy, because brothers go to jail and get shot over it; no knowledge, because the priest's lips are not teaching it. By swearing, and lying, the complete lies we heard two weeks ago from a man claiming nobody told him to leave the sister alone, corrected in front of everybody; and killing, and stealing, as in the videos; and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood. David saw Bathsheba and lost it all. The Lord gave a dress code because he knows what happens when the clothes come off. Full of wickedness is literal, and backdoor marriages produce it. You will do it right or not at all.
precepts.point: That is exactly why the enemy goes after the daughters: mess up the women and the children are done, because they are the ones with the kids. Willie Lynch called her the most valuable commodity for that reason. Once she is whored out by all kinds of men, her value and self-esteem are gone and she lays with any man who smiles at her, as the 65-year-old at Mardi Gras. Then the land falls to whoredom, women giving their bodies with no scrutiny to sweet words, and the land becomes full of wickedness, everything about what feels good now. I am only talking about it; your children are living it, and you had better be glad someone is telling you.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders & Fathers: the Children Are Listening

precepts.why:
Leviticus warns that if a daughter is prostituted, “the land become full of wickedness.” Hosea shows what full of wickedness looks like: “Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” Controversy means against: the Lord is against how we live. It speaks mainly of the northern kingdom, but all of us are doing this now.

No truth: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” Truth is the Bible, the laws. Nobody in the land is adhering to “Do not prostitute thy daughter”; nobody is paying attention to it or bringing that precaution into the land. No mercy: people get killed over this. Brothers have gone to jail and been shot down over it. No knowledge of God, meaning his commandments: the priest's lips should keep knowledge and the people should seek the law at his mouth, and they are not getting it at all.

“By swearing, and lying”. We heard complete lies two weeks ago: a man told everybody that nobody had told him to leave the sister alone, to make it look as if the leadership didn't know what was going on. Brothers had to stand up, bring him right back to his lying statement, and correct his wicked ass in front of everybody, so nobody would think he had a toe to stand on to justify the evil he did. Then: “and killing, and stealing”: we saw that in the videos.

All of it because the woman was taught to let her behind hang out. The Bible gives a dress code: cover your ass. The Lord gave a dress code because he knows that when the clothes come off, all kinds of things go on. David saw Bathsheba, and he lost it all. Then: “and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood”. People get stabbed and shot up, all because she had her clothes off in the street. Do you see the connection?

So “full of wickedness” means literally full of wickedness: that is what you get when God's laws are not taught, no Bible, no scruples, no laws. Having kids through backdoor marriages produces madness like this. That is done here. You're going to do it right or you ain't going to do it at all; nobody is holding a ceremony over fornication. It starts with the fathers and mothers, who must not prostitute the daughter, because the enemy goes after the women: mess them up and the children are done.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Christ “must needs go through Samaria”, to Sychar, “near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph”, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh. The woman of Samaria said, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” The Samaritans were the northern kingdom, and the Jews had no dealings with them because of that beef from way back.

Hosea is where it came from: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” The Lord said leave them alone, they're joined to idols, and Judah took that as okay: what the hell with them, they're cast off. But Judah forgot the part where it said they would be joined together and appoint themselves one head. That was dismissed because of the hatred the houses had for each other, that back and forth.

Yet the woman said, “Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well”? She called Jacob our father, and Joseph's house got that well: she was Israel. She said “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”, Gerizim, where all Israel worshipped before Jerusalem. And Isaiah said “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel. And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria”, so she said “I know that Messias cometh”.

The disciples “marvelled that he talked with the woman”, because the Jews didn't deal with the northern kingdom. But those are our people. Christ taught the Samaritans two days, and they knew “that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world”: the world is Israel. The dividing hatred said let him alone, but Christ came to heal it.

precepts.text: The priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth.
precepts.point: That which is highly esteemed among men, like shellfish and bacon, is abomination in the sight of God.

note.label: 2025 Recap: Different Times, Same Truth

precepts.why:
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge”. What is the knowledge we have rejected? Malachi answers: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth”. The knowledge is the law.

So the knowledge is not what you learn at a university; the black woman is the most educated woman on the earth, and that is not the knowledge we are ignorant of. Our people are ignorant of the laws of God. Our people don't understand that today is the Lord's Sabbath, and you are not supposed to be buying and selling, cooking, or playing football, because the white man said every day is the Sabbath. Our women don't understand they are not supposed to wear pants, because that knowledge was taken from them. Our men in America don't know they are not supposed to shave their beards, because the white man said, if you want to look like a man, shave your beard.

We are in a diabolical matrix, deeper than anything the movie could show: everything you were taught is good here in America is bad. That is why Hosea goes on, “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.” That is what has happened to us. Our people are at the bottom of society, the mother with her kids living all year for a tax return, the drug dealers, the ball players and the rappers, all in Esau's trick bag, while the man down the street teaching the law is what would disrupt all of it.

precepts.text: That which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.
precepts.point: That which is highly esteemed among men, like shellfish and bacon, is abomination in the sight of God.

note.label: 2025 Recap: Different Times, Same Truth

precepts.why:
Everything the white man taught us is good here is bad. If you really want to go all out for your wife or your girlfriend, you buy lobster, the delicacy. The Bible says that is the scum of the earth. They have you paying $200 for a fat roach, eating clams and clam chowder, bottom feeders, rodents of the sea, and spending your hard-earned check to do it. You want to upscale a burger, put bacon on it. All of these things are abominable to God, and God is looking at us like, they have you in a trick bag. We are living in the upside-down.

Christ said it: “Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.” That which is highly esteemed among men is everything Esau and the nations put above God.

Justifying yourselves before men is the brothers and sisters who know the truth, who know what we are saying is right and will even say Jesus is black, but won't serve God, won't come out of the pagan holidays, and won't keep the commandments. God knows the heart.

That is how our people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. We have taken what men esteem, the Sunday, the shaved face, the shellfish and the bacon, over the law of our God, and calling a bottom feeder a delicacy makes absolutely no sense. The knowledge we rejected is the laws of God.

precepts.text: Certain ungodly persons, who hated their own people, went unto the king.
precepts.point: There is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land. Evil was among Israel before the white man; it only multiplied under him.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
When the Greeks came into power, the evils of our people multiplied, the same evils that were already among us in Moses' time. First Maccabees shows it: “Then came ungodly persons, who hated their own people, went unto the king, and told him that Jonathan besieged the tower”. Our own people, who hated their people, ran to Massa to tell on our brother Jonathan, who loved his people. Rats.

And Hosea 4:1 is before the Europeans came into power at all. “Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land”: he is talking to Israelites in our own land, and his issue is with us. “because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” No truth, no laws, no mercy or kindness among our people. We were being evil: “By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” Brother kills brother, brother kills sister, sister kills sister.

“Therefore shall the land mourn”: God said, I am going to take away all your resources, and have the heathen come in, destroy you and take your possessions, because of all the evil you are doing among yourselves.

Black folks love to point the finger and say the white man made us evil. No. Evil was always among us; it just multiplied when we got around this man. All skinfolk ain't kinfolk: those ungodly persons who hated their own people and ran to the king were our own, and they still are.

precepts.text: I will give it into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth.
precepts.point: There is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land. Evil was among Israel before the white man; it only multiplied under him.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
Even in the Israelite nation you have evil ones. “As for the beauty of his ornament, he set it in majesty: but they made the images of their abominations and of their detestable things therein: therefore have I set it far from them.” We were sacrificing to idols, worshipping other gods and violating God's laws.

“And I will give it into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a spoil; and they shall pollute it.” God gave our land and our sanctuary into the hands of other nations, starting with the Babylonians, and to the wicked of the earth: that is Edom, the European man. “My face will I turn also from them”: you ask for my help and I am not listening. “for the robbers shall enter into it, and defile it.” The robbers are still there; they call themselves Israelis today. Imagine a robber who robs your house and never leaves: he posts up, puts your ass in the basement, and when someone asks whose picture that is of a black man, he says, that's me, I had a tan that day.

“Make a chain: for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.” Make a chain means judgment was established. What is crime? Sin. We became a nation of criminals, and a criminal gets incarcerated; we are still serving our sentence today. Some will stay in prison till it burns, and some will get out on good behaviour, keeping God's commandments. Our cities were full of violence before any white intervention, and we are the answer to our own problems.

“Wherefore I will bring the worst of the heathen, and they shall possess their houses”: the worst of all the nations God made, and we are under him now. He possessed our lands, our people and our identity. “I will also make the pomp of the strong to cease”: we were prideful, sure nothing would happen to us and we would be in the land forever. “Destruction cometh; and they shall seek peace, and there shall be none.” We seek peace, equality and rights, and there is none, because we were rebellious then and we are worse now.

precepts.text: They burn incense under oaks and poplars and elms, and your spouses commit adultery.
precepts.point: Groves of trees are where the nations worshipped, and powerful men still gather at such places.

note.label: Christmas/ Icons, Idolatry, White Supremacy !!revealed!!

precepts.why:
Hosea shows what went on under those trees: “They sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains, and burn incense upon the hills, under oaks and poplars and elms”. Oaks and poplars and elms are green trees, the same groves Exodus 34:13 says to cut down.

Why under the trees? “because the shadow thereof is good”. That owl in the Bohemian Grove sits under the shadow of those trees in the picture. The shadow of the tree is good to them because the idol is under the tree.

Then the fruit of it: “therefore your daughters shall commit whoredom, and your spouses shall commit adultery”. Around that owl they visit, they do all kinds of sexual rituals; sexual things take place around that owl at Bohemian Grove. All the presidents, including Obama, who y'all love so much, went there, and who knows what was going on over there.

So the groves were not harmless. The worship under the green tree brings whoredom and adultery with it, and that is why God commanded Israel to cut them down.

precepts.text: Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone. So at one point northern kingdom were not a part of the commonwealth of Israel. Why? They became strangers. They became alienated from the commonwealth of Israel. Very basic and simple. All you have to do is read. Blessed is he that readeth.
precepts.point: Strangers. Strangers. Now, the literal definition of Gentiles is nation. How can you in time past be another nation? How can you in time past be another race? Go to sleep Japanese, wake up Arab. That does not make any sense. But when you are dealing with Christianity, it makes all the sense in the world.

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
Why were Ephraim and the northern kingdom called strangers? Hosea says it: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.”

So at one point the northern kingdom was not a part of the commonwealth of Israel. Why? Ephraim joined himself to idols and was let alone. They became strangers; they became alienated from the commonwealth of Israel. That is what Paul means by “aliens from the commonwealth of Israel”: not another race of people, but Israelites who were cut off for their idolatry.

It is very basic and simple. All you have to do is read. Blessed is he that readeth.

precepts.point: They raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; wherefore the name of that place was called the valley of Achor unto this day.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee”. We quote that often, but the end of the verse we seldom quote says, “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.”

That is why the scripture says all Israel “burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones”: them, because his household went with him. Achan’s sons and daughters did not steal the garment, the silver or the wedge of gold, yet because he lacked knowledge and understanding they paid for the covetous spirit he carried. His selfish, individual spirit never weighed what his family would pay; he was the reason men died in that battle and the nation was nearly overtaken.

The Lord hits where it hurts. Your sin reaches your children, your wife, your husband, your brothers and sisters. Reject knowledge and the Lord will reject thee, and he will forget thy children too.

precepts.text: The Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land; keep the laws so the controversy is not with you.
precepts.point: The Most High hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land; if you do not want the Lord to have a controversy with you, keep the laws. And keeping the laws is more than beards, fringes, borders of blue, and not eating pork: it is purging the unfruitful spirits you know dwell inside you, the jealousy, envy, covetousness, malice, hatred, grudging, backbiting, murmuring, and gossip.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why:
Joshua wrote upon the stones “a copy of the law of Moses” in the presence of all the children of Israel. “Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” If you do not want the Lord to have a controversy with you, keep the laws.

And keeping the laws is more than beards, fringes, borders of blue, and not eating pork. It is purging the unfruitful spirits you know dwell inside you: the jealousy, envy, covetousness, malice, hatred, grudging, backbiting, murmuring and gossip.

precepts.text: The people are destroyed for lack of knowledge, and because they rejected the knowledge of the law, the Most High rejects them.
precepts.point: He will forsake the remnant of His inheritance and deliver them into the hand of their enemies to be a prey and a spoil, because they have provoked Him to anger since the day their fathers came out of Egypt. The Most High has borne with this wickedness for hundreds of years.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

precepts.why:
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee”, “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.”

Because Judah rejected the knowledge of the law, the Most High rejects them: “I will forsake the remnant of mine inheritance, and deliver them into the hand of their enemies.” They have provoked him to anger “since the day their fathers came forth out of Egypt, even unto this day.” He bore with this wickedness for hundreds of years, and now it is rejection for rejection.

precepts.text: The Most High has a controversy with the land for lying, killing, and stealing, black on black crime, so the land mourns and everyone in it languishes.
precepts.point: Day and night they go about seeking violence; wickedness is in the midst and deceit and guile depart not from her streets.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
“Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land. By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” The Most High has a controversy with the land for the lying, killing and stealing, black on black crime, blood touching blood. That is the violence and strife David saw in the city, the mischief and sorrow in the midst of it.

“Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein shall languish, with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of heaven; yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be taken away.” The land mourns and everyone in it languishes. This is us cursed in the city.

precepts.text: Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.
precepts.point: The Jews in that day were Judah, Benjamin and Levi, not all twelve tribes. The Samaritans were Ephraim, and the reason for the separation is written in the prophets.

note.label: John 4: The Woman at the Well and the Nobleman's Son

precepts.why:
“Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” That is why the Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans. The Samaritans were Ephraim, and Ephraim was joined to idols, and the word was to let him alone.

So the woman's question, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria?”, comes out of that history in the prophets: Ephraim broken, joined to idols, let alone by Judah.

precepts.text: Ephraim is joined to idols; let him alone, which is why the prophets would not deal with the north.
precepts.point: Isaiah then prophesied that because Ephraim conspired with Syria, Ephraim would be broken within sixty-five years so that it would be "not a people," and Hosea said the same, that Ephraim was joined to idols and would get no more mercy but be utterly taken away and carried into Assyria. Broken and removed from the land, they lost their nationality, culture, and heritage and were assimilated into the nations.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.”

That is why the prophets would not deal with the north. Ephraim was joined to the idols Jeroboam set up, the calves in Bethel and Dan, and the word was to let him alone. Judah kept that word, and it hardened into the wall Peter speaks of.

note.label: From Negroes to Gods from Earth to Gold

points: Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land. Because there is no truth: the application of God's law is not being applied. There is no mercy being shown, nor knowledge of God in the land. Our people have no knowledge of God, so it is our job to bring them back. There is no knowledge of God because the laws of God are not being taught, or enforced.

As people are coming in, they are buying into the system. They believe that they are the Israelites. They believe what is being taught is true. The word of God must be applied. Here is one simple law that is not negotiable: remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. How do you keep the Sabbath day holy? We must congregate. We cannot cook, we cannot buy, we cannot sell on the Lord's Sabbath day. It is a holy convocation. There is no way around that. You cannot decide not to do that. It is those small things, the application of God's laws, that separate us. We cannot reason it in our minds. The Lord said, I seek such that are going to worship me as it is written, in spirit and truth.

So what if for the Sabbath I decide, or anyone decides, not to congregate with the body, or to congregate partially, but then congregate with somebody that has been put out of the body? They would be sinning. It might seem, you know why people would do that? Because again, we rationalise in our minds what we think is acceptable and God will be all right with. God said, No, my commandments are straight. This is what I told you to do. That is our biggest problem, that we try to put our thoughts in on how it should be done. The Lord said, Your thoughts are not my thoughts. I told you it is a holy convocation. Do what I tell you to do. And it is not hard. It is only when we start to try to rationalise in our minds.
